title: Host announce fanout causes intermittent tenant isolation flap and DNS blackholing
creator: Ava Patel
description:
Summary:
Several Dedicated customers reported intermittent inability to resolve private hostnames after peering failovers and GPU pool resizes. Symptoms manifested as tenant-level DNS blackholing and transient egress isolation that recovered without VM-level restarts. Multiple escalations came in between 2026-03-09 and 2026-03-10; impacted tenants had service disruptions for short windows (30s-5m) and saw spike in 5xxs when backend calls timed out.

Investigation highlights:
- Reproduced by triggering controlled peering reshuffle in staging under load and by simulating host announce storms during a node scale-down.
- Root cause: an orthogonal control-plane change (host announce fanout optimization) introduced aggressive announce batching with a shared reconciliation epoch counter. Under high churn the epoch counter could be recycled by a new host announce, which caused a small window where egress resolver entries were marked stale but not reconciled by the tenant-specific SNAT/route reconciliation worker. DNS queries during that window were routed to a default resolver that returned NXDOMAIN or to a stale resolver IP outside the tenant's VPC.
- Contributing factors: (1) delayed control-plane reconciliation backoffs, (2) a separate GC path that removed resolver bindings after a soft timeout when epoch mismatch was detected, (3) insufficient e2e test coverage for peering flaps with simultaneous host announce bursts.

Customers impacted:
- 3 Dedicated customers (one enterprise, two mid-market), support escalations opened with priority. All customers are using Dedicated with cross-VPC peering and custom resolver mappings. No data exfiltration observed; impact was availability and DNS correctness.

Mitigation applied (customer-facing, short-term):
- Immediate rollback of the aggressive host announce batching optimization in the control plane at 2026-03-10 22:40 UTC (rolled to canary then global).
- Temporary increase of resolver-binding TTLs and disablement of the GC path that pruned stale bindings during epoch transitions. This reduced blast radius while we developed the fix.

Permanent fix implemented (branch/runtime-PRs):
- Adjust reconciliation semantics: bind resolver entries to per-tenant epoch tokens and make the SNAT/route reconcilers resilient to transient epoch reuse by gating GC on last-successful-reconcile timestamp instead of epoch equality.
- Add a linearizable update to the binding table write path so host announce updates cannot create ephemeral unreferenced bindings.
- Introduced backoff jitter to the host-announce fanout code to avoid synchronized bursts across hosts.
- End-to-end test harness added: synthetic peering reshuffle generator that simulates host announce storms + KV cache churn and asserts resolver binding continuity.

Testing and verification:
- Staging stress run: 24h with continuous peering reshuffles under production-like QPS, zero DNS resolution failures for tenant-scoped names observed in 10k sample queries per minute.
- Canary rollout: deployed to 5% of Dedicated clusters for 6 hours, then 25% for 12 hours, then full roll. Monitoring showed reduction in short-term DNS failures to baseline.

Rollout plan:
- runtime-1.26 release contains the fix. Scheduled cluster rollout starting 2026-03-14 with planned maintenance windows for Dedicated tenants (rolling, no VM restarts). Ops runbook updated with verification steps.

Follow-ups and action items:
- Improve observability: add per-tenant resolver binding lifecycle metrics and an alert when >0.1% of tenants observe resolver rebind failures in a 5m window. Owner: SRE (Janelle Ortiz).
- Hardening: add formal property-based tests for host announce concurrency in the serving runtime and include peering reshuffle scenarios in nightly CI. Owner: Marcus Li.
- Customer communication: product sent incident summary and mitigation timeline to affected customers and offered SLA credits where appropriate. Owner: Sylvie Martin (Support).

References:

- PRs: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1287 (epoch-fix), https://github.com/redwood-inference/control-plane/pull/842 (fanout-jitter-disable)
